## PR #135: after-deploy cost reading

Deployment: **PID 21832**, source build **bb753b8fa3786eb7ec4cc90603de095fa242bd5d**, per pm-001's merge/bounce record. Main independently matched that revision. Both ping snapshots were healthy, reporting PID 21832 and `pij-rs 0.1.0` (not an embedded Git SHA). Process observations confirmed the same executable and start time, **2026-11-07 22:33:25 +10:00**, throughout.

| Metric | AFTER |
|---|---|
| Daemon launches | **178 to 178: +0 / 60.001418 s = 0.000/s** |
| Machine-wide launches | **83.0/s**, niced 20.0 s sample |
| Daemon CPU | **7.58 CPU seconds / 60.001418 s = 12.63%** of one CPU over the interval |
| Daemon RSS | **136,384 to 136,800 KiB = 133.19 to 133.59 MiB** |
| Load averages | Start **13.06 / 10.99 / 10.10**, end **12.63 / 11.16 / 10.21** |

Window: **2026-11-07 22:36:44.696996 to 22:37:44.698680 +10:00**, elapsed measured monotonically between snapshot starts. Endpoint `ps` CPU percentages were **7.6% and 5.0%**, distinct from the cumulative-CPU interval result.

### Every recorded daemon site was flat

| Operation | Delta |
|---|---:|
| `ddocs.community` | 0 |
| `gh.delivered` | 0 |
| `git.community` | 0 |
| `git.pa-watchdog-common-dir` | 0 |
| `ps.registration-native-process` | 0 |
| `ps.sidecar-process-group` | 0 |
| `tmux.control-client` | 0 |
| `tmux.new-window` | 0 |
| `tmux.pipe-pane attach` | 0 |
| `tmux.rename-window` | 0 |
| `tmux.set-options tap owner` | 0 |
| **Total** | **0** |

Per-site deltas sum to the total; no counter decrease or PID/start-time change occurred. Positive baseline counters verify the launch instrument was populated, not unavailable. The earlier all-reloaded #145 window on PID 28490/build c3895da also had zero daemon launches; that is a separate historical quiet window, not a matched #135 CPU/RSS BEFORE.

### Machine coverage and interpretation

Ran `nice -n 19 just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json` from deployed main in parallel with the daemon window. Independent listening-port discovery also identified PID 21832. It reported **83.0 new PIDs/s** and **82.9 sampled/s**, with attribution lower bounds **56.0/s other** and **26.9/s gone before inspection**. No direct-daemon-child category was observed. Lower bounds and this shorter window must not be equated to the daemon's 60-second counters.

Visible command lower bounds included bash **31.2/s**, git-ai **12.6/s**, copilot **6.2/s** and node **2.1/s**. The probe itself made **256,739 in-process libproc polls** and runs niced but busy-polling; machine CPU/load is not unperturbed.

**Requested AFTER reading complete.** No recorded daemon launch producer advanced in this window, but daemon CPU was not zero. It includes existing background duties; this reading does not attribute that CPU to a particular loop or prove a regression improvement. No matched CPU/RSS BEFORE was supplied for #135.

The scratch-role retirement dogfood preceded this window; no edit/retire/merge operation was manufactured during it. Flat Git/ddocs counters and a quiet window are not benchmarks of role-gate contention, large-backlog notices/withdrawal, retarget generation or routes rebuild. Those qualifications in the verdict remain.

Raw receipts are retained as session evidence (`pr135-after-window.json`, `pr135-after-machine.json`). The reusable `daemon-cost-window.py` records same-incarnation counter and cumulative-CPU deltas. No builds, tests, stress traffic, source edits or daemon restart were performed.
